questions.knowledge_point: Finding the X-Intercepts of a Hyperbola
questions.problem:
From **left to right,** the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola $\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=1$ are

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $)\,$
and 
$\,($
{{field-3}}, 
{{field-4}} $).$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{16}-\frac{(0)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ {x}^{2} & =16 \\ x & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the $x$-intercepts are $(-4,0)$ and $(4,0).$

questions.problem:
The $x$-intercept of the hyperbola $\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}=1$ is$\,(${{field-1}},
{{field-2}}$).$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{(0-3)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ 1-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4} & =0 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =0 \\ x-2 & =0 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercept is $(2,0).$

questions.problem: Calculate the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola $\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{9}=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(0)^{2}}{3}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ -\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

We cannot take the square root of a negative number. Therefore, the equation has no real solutions. So, there are no $x$-intercepts.

$$

questions.problem: Calculate the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola $\frac{(y+5)^{2}}{5}-(x-2)^{2}=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y+5)^{2}}{5}-(x-2)^{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(y+5)^{2}}{5}-(0-2)^{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(y+5)^{2}}{5}-4 & =1 \\ \frac{(y+5)^{2}}{5} & =5 \\ (y+5)^{2} & =25 \\ y+5 & =\pm 5 \\ y & =-10,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercepts are $(0,-10)$ and $(0,0).$

questions.problem: Calculate the points where the hyperbola $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=1$ intersects the line $x=-1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $x=-1,$ we substitute $x=-1$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{1}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ -\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ {y}^{2} & =-\frac{27}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We cannot take the square root of a negative number. Therefore, the equation has no real solutions. 
So, the hyperbola does not intersect the vertical line $x=-1.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{10}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{25} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+1)^{2}}{10}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{25} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+1)^{2}}{10} & =1 \\ (x+1)^{2} & =10 \\ x+1 & =\pm \sqrt{10} \\ x & =-1\pm \sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts are $\left(-1\pm \sqrt{10},0\right).$

canonical_examples.problem:
Calculate the points where the hyperbola 
$\dfrac{x^2}{10}-\dfrac{y^2}{15}=1$
intersects the line $y=-3.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=-3,$ we substitute $y=-3$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{10}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{15} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{10}-\frac{(-3)^{2}}{15} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{10}-\frac{9}{15} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{10}-\frac{3}{5} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}-6 & =10 \\ {x}^{2} & =16 \\ x & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the hyperbola intersects the horizontal line $y=-3$ at the points $(\pm 4, -3).$
